utterances.text: Therefore, you still believe that the part pertaining to the guards brigade in this report is incorrect, whereas the other portions are?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Attached units defined from which formations they came.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask you the following: The 20th Partisan Brigade was within OG South, it wasn't attached to the guards brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And the units we are discussing now, being attached to the guards brigade, they were attached to it directly. Does it tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps. The artillery battalions were subordinated to the guards brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude that given the explanations, this would reflect the situation on the 16th of November?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In your testimony in chief yesterday you explained the objections put by Major Tesic who was commander of the 1st Assault Detachment as regarded combat actions carried out by his subordinate units when it came to the local TO and volunteers, and he complained that because of their failure to implement their tasks he was unable to develop his activities according to the plan of OG South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way he usually justified the failures to carry out fully the plans put forward by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Therefore, there were discipline issues in carrying out military tasks, but what my learned friend asked you yesterday, perhaps you will remember, that whether he reported any lack of discipline as regarded the maltreatment of civilians or prisoners, or whether the lack of discipline pertained only to the failure to carry out combat tasks and protection -- the protection of property?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As -- when it comes to combat activities, as I explained to the OTP, when it came to implementing the tasks assigned by the commander, they reported they had difficulty because of the lack of motivation and in discipline of the members of the TO. That's the way he reported. Whether that was true or not, that can be explained by the commander. When it comes to the maltreatment of civilians by members of the TO, he never reported anything on that, because there was no need to. Later on he did report something to that effect when the incidents began taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You mean the incidents mentioned on the 18th, 19th and the 20th, the insults, the abuse?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But everyone came in and reported more or less the same thing, and I've explained the flow of information. But since we're discussing Tesic and the Assault Detachment No. 1 and the implementation of tasks, that's when he spoke about the lack of motivation and all the other elements we've mentioned, and his failure to comply with the commander's orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday in chief you also stated that some sort of revenge could be expected by the local population, but would we -- could we agree that it all boiled down to verbal abuse and an occasional kick or a slap, something that was insufficient to raise any suspicion that killings may occur?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I link that up with the principle of foresight. A true commander can foresee things. And I answered precisely to -- to the OTP attorney that it should have been foreseen, and that judging by all the information received, that should have sufficed to signal that even serious things could take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that all the information that came in boiled down to verbal abuse or light physical contact, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: All that information should have served as a basis for an assessment of what may come in the future?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way I put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have Exhibit 425 shown on the screen, please? And I will have questions for the witness. And I think I have it in the tab binder. That is tab 35. It is a regular combat report by the command of OG South dated the 22nd November, 1991. Mr. Trifunovic, do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the last two paragraphs of the report?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During the day all measures have been taken related to the 80th Motorised Brigade taking over the organisational and commanding functions of in the area of the responsibility of the Operations Group South. The command of the 80th Motorised Brigade received instructions and documents regarding the organisation of command and control in the area of responsibility of OG South."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Based on military regulation, this statement that the 80th Motorised Brigade was given all instructions and documents needed to organise command and control in the area of responsibility of OG South, does that actually mean that there was a handover of all the documents pertaining to command and control?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handing over of an area of responsibility or of the duties comprises several segments, and there is a plan to be made. This particular element of handing over the documents usually comes last, but not necessarily. It could include the last tour of the area or of the positions, and so on and so forth. That's what could come last; but again, not necessarily. Usually does. We've seen everything and now we hand over the documents. That was the practice. But this was combat, so it could have been different.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Some other actions had to be taken in terms of the handover before the documents were handed over?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So the handover began before that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It had to. This is the last task in the process of handover of responsibility for a certain zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Trifunovic. Could you please tell me when did you find out in OG South, or in the Guards Motorised Brigade, about what happened at Ovcara? Could you tell me? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I tell you when you're asking me when did you from the command? Are you asking me? I apologise, but you should ask me directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: All right. When did you find out?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out when the indictment was issued against Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And before that at the brigade command or for as long as you were in Vukovar, or on your return to Belgrade, you didn't hear anything about it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The OG South command did not receive any kind of written report about an incident involving the 80th Motorised Brigade, about what had happened at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the level that I was involved or that I had knowledge of, no, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Had something like that arrived, it would have been recorded in the war diary, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. The commander would have been informed and all of the organs would have known. Everybody in the command would have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: My colleague asked you whether the Guards Motorised Brigade, when it arrived in Belgrade carried out any kind of investigation about the events at Ovcara. What I would like to ask is: Would you agree with me that the guards brigade should not have carried out an investigation, but the 80th Motorised Brigade, because it happened in its territory and it stayed as the command in Vukovar after the guards brigade left for Belgrade, as well as the unit which, according to the resubordination order, was -- had TO Vukovar as its subordinate unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether any actions were carried out while the guards brigade was still in Vukovar. I answered yes, because investigative organs were sent from the superior command in view of the fact that the guards brigade did not have such personnel. That's what he asked me. He didn't ask me whether any measures were taken on its return to Belgrade. Now you can ask me the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did the 80th Motorised Brigade, which remained in Vukovar as the local command, have the possibility of carrying out an investigation about what had happened in its area of responsibility by units that were subordinate to it or resubordinated to it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, in the document by commander of OG South, it states that investigation organs from the 1st Military District should be assisted by the 80th Motorised Brigade. As to which sector, that was not specified. They came to OG South commander, and he ordered the 80th Brigade to offer assistance, to receive them, accommodate them, provide soldiers, provide security, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This group for clearing the terrain was headed by Colonel Basic. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard something. At the time I did know that. Later I forgot. The meeting with him was conducted by Colonel Panic and they said why they had come. I think I recorded that also in the diary, although I did not attend the meeting. Lieutenant-Colonel Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you mentioned in response to a question by my learned friend that command -- the commander told you to prepare a document on the 20th of November about the appointment of Vujovic as commander of the Vukovar TO. Did the command -- can a commander of the JNA appoint a TO commander, or is that in the jurisdiction of somebody else?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I asked myself the same thing, but I did carry out the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You also told my learned friend that you never saw whether this order was signed, and you don't know what happened to it.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was signed. What I said was that I didn't know when it was signed and what the dead-lines were for Miroljub Vujovic to assume this duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When was the order signed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was signed. I was ordered, or the order was issued to me on the 20th, so I don't know whether it was on the -- in the evening of the 20th or in the morning of the 21st. I don't have that order. All I know is that I was ordered to write, and I wrote what was asked of me. I don't know if I took it for signature that evening or in the morning. I really don't remember. The order was signed; that's what I do know. I cannot recall any other details of the order other than that Vujovic was assigned as commander of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did -- was the order registered in view of the fact that it is not in accordance with the regulations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could have been registered in the documents log.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, did you not tell my learned friend that Miroljub Vujovic, once you had already arrived in Vukovar, was already the commander of the TO?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said. I said that he was the commander of the TO detachment Petrova Gora. Detachment. The TO of Vukovar, well, Vukovar is a large town. There were about 10 units at the level of a detachment, they had their rear units. Who was the commander; I heard that that was Jaksic. When the TO broke up, probably in the course of 1991 --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You said that it had rear units. I don't think that that's in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not talking about the defence of Vukovar, Mr. Vasic. I was talking about the TO detachment Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you what you said just now about the TO. You said that they had rear organs, and that is not in the transcript. That was my intervention.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the structure of the Territorial Defence of a town of the kind of Vukovar, as I said, at that time, when it was normal, it had to have had about 10 units, the type of brigade detachments, the TO of a town, the broader socio-political community, and a commander of a fairly high rank, all the elements. This was just one section of it at Petrova Gora, just one detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you talked about the visit by Vojislav Seselj in the area of responsibility in the zone of operations of OG South. What I would like to know is whether Vojislav Seselj could have received permission to enter the zone from the 1st Military District or from the federal secretary for national defence, was the permission issued in Sid, and whether the command of OG South just needed to be informed about who was actually entering its zone of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In practice what would happen with his visits is something that I really don't know. Who authorised him or issued permission for him to do that, I don't know that. But as far as the procedure is concerned, I'm sure some people could explain how that went. All I heard was that he came, that he was at Petrova Gora, that he was in the Assault Detachment 1, that he was raising morale, working on the motivation, and I think that Colonel Mrksic did not issue a permission for that either. Perhaps when he found out he was just reconciled to the fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that permission to enter was issued at Sid, not only for military officers, but also for journalists and all of those who wanted to enter the area. This is something that we heard from journalists.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's not something that I really thought about, but I remember that I was told when somebody came that it was necessary to receive a permit, because the -- there was a check-point or an office of the 1st Military District in Sid. But as I mentioned, such bases were organised in different places for OG South. So you could not just enter the area of OG South just like that, it had to be with the signed permission of a commander of the 1st Military District. That was the way that you could have access to the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes, now it's quite clear how the whole thing functioned. These documents now that you talked about, the war diary, the log-book, the register of documents, orders and reports that were received by telephone, the briefings book, where were these documents kept? Were they kept in any particular place by the operations group, and the guards brigade? Was there any particular place where these documents were being kept?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- they were all kept at the command in Negoslavci in the operations room. They were kept in a -- in a casket under key, or a locker.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you returned to Belgrade after the 24th of November, do you know where the documents were kept?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. They were kept at the premises of the brigade, together with the combat plan, the plan for use of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to know if, as part of the documents that were being maintained in Vukovar by the guards brigade, there was a log of operations maintained as well, because there is a duty to keep such a log-book?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that we did keep such a document too, but I didn't really check that document particularly, and I really cannot recall its contents, but I do know that there was such a document that was being maintained.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know who maintained the operations log-book, and was that also recorded in the operations room?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. And it was done by some of the duty officers. I don't know who it was though, because they were constantly out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you were on duty at the guards brigade, did you ever see this operations diary or log-book?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my return from Vukovar, when this -- these documents were stored properly at the war room with the plan for use, I really never showed any interest in these documents. I never wanted to see them. I was not informed about the war plan for Vukovar. That was not in my jurisdiction, that was in the jurisdiction of the Chief of Staff. I was never Chief of Staff, therefor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the Chief of Staff is the one who deals with these documents, and he is the one who uses all the documents that happened to be in the war room?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The war room is locked and access to it is available only to the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The specific conditions in the guards brigade were exactly like that. The plan of mobilisation and a plan of utilisation were kept in the war room. And the special units corps documents and the guards brigade documents were all kept in the same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But since Vukovar you didn't have the opportunity to see the operations log-book?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the operations log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us: This register of received and dispatched orders, did you have an opportunity to see that from the time of Vukovar until now?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the Prosecutor's office asked the guards brigade to provide documents from the archives, I was Deputy Commander then, and I was in Vukovar, and I was also the president of that commission, so I did find the log-book in the archives, and we sent it. All that we found in the archives, we provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Is this the archive meaning this war room that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the archive from the war room where the Vukovar archives were also kept. I don't want to go into the particular problems that we had after the bombing. There was a hit on that part, so a part of the archive was saved, and that was reported to the Ministry of Defence, so they do have information about what else is in that archive, since it is still being kept at the guards brigade, I was there a month ago, I was always chairman of that commission, so I do know what's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But the operations log is not there, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, but I can't remember specifically. Maybe it is there. Nobody ever asked about it, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: There is just another thing that I would like to ask you. Do you perhaps remember this: There was that order by the commander of the 1st Military District, 1614-82/81, the 18th of November, 1991, Exhibit 415 at tab 24. What about after this order? Was there not another order from the commander of the 1st Military District to evacuate the Vukovar Hospital, 1614-82/72?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said 24, the 18th of November, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes. We don't have the whole number, so I'll just repeat. We discussed this order, you explained about it. But I want to know something else. There's reference here to an order for OG South in coordination with TG 7 to enter the Vukovar Hospital. What I want to know is after this order, was there another order from the command of the 1st Military District on the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital? And the number is strictly confidential 1614-82/82, dated the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Unless it was actually produced by the security organ who themselves arrived on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for all your answers, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies. I may want to take another five seconds of your time. On page 55, line 14, instead of TG 7, it should read TG north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I am Borivoje Borovic on behalf of Miroslav Radic. Before I begin, I would like to have the usher's assistance, please. I have a hard copy of a document and I would like to have this handed to the witness, just in case we use it or tender it. They will be displayed on our screens, but I wish to hurry things along in terms of the procedural aspects. Secondly, there is another copy for the Prosecutor and three copies for the benefit of the Chamber. The green markings only mean that these documents have already been tendered and admitted. The red markings or tabs mean that I will be tendering these. I think this will help us to expedite this cross-examination. Before we begin, I would like to have the Chamber's attention briefly, please. We had a small matter of the English translation, something to do with our terminology at the beginning. I'm afraid we might encounter the same problem today, and we might deal with this in the following way: This is about the distinction between "komandir" and "komandant." A komandir is up to company level; and a komandant is up from battalion level. We shall be using the original terms from B/C/S, since there are no clear English equivalents. We shall be using komandir for a company commander, and komandant for battalion commander. This will prove of significance later on when a military expert starts analysing all the military documents. We shall immediately realise that there is a huge distinction between these two, komandir and komandant. Komandir referring to a company level and down; and komandant referring to battalion level and up. I'm sure the witness will help us clarify this matter further, but I thought it might be a good idea to draw the Chamber's attention to the issue right at the outset.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My first question: During your testimony in chief, you talked about the importance of a proper functioning of the system of command and control in units and anywhere else in the armed forces, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I would like to now immediately raise this issue that I told the Chamber about. Can you please draw a basic distinction between the concepts of komandir and komandant, so that the Chamber understands what my question is about? If you have an officer who is in command of a company, the title used is komandir. If you have an officer in charge of a battalion, or any other higher level unit, the term used is komandant. Can you please explain the distinction between these two, a company commander and a battalion commander, or any other high-ranking unit. What is the difference between these?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Detachment, squad and company belong to a tactical level, to something that we refer to as lower tactical level. From battalion level up to brigade level, we speak of a higher tactical level. It is only logical that the term komandir should refer to lower level tactical units and the term komandant refers to exercising command over these higher level tactical units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that komandant, the term komandant, is used only in relation to higher level tactical units, but never in relation to a company, for example?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would it be fair to say that in all combat operations the komandants set up command posts and company commanders set up observation posts?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't get your answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We've heard a number of witnesses here saying that a company commander has the staff within his combat disposition from which allegedly he exercises command. Can you tell us what a staff is and what is the first established -- establishment in terms of organisation that a staff sets up during combat operations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A staff is part of a brigade command. Unifying all the different aspects of command at a particular level. The first next organizational unit that a staff has attached to it is a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that a company commander cannot set up a staff at his observation post?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that follows logically, doesn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When a company commander issues a task to his subordinates during an attack on a populated area, now this is a question for you as a renowned military expert. What does he do? Does he issue an order to attack on the spot, in purely practical terms, how does that work?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the spot, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: During what is usually referred to as command reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During command reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with the Defence when we say that there are no meetings with the various units that the operations are -- that are involved in the operation? The only thing that happens is he meets them on the spot and issues his instructions, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Your introduction was somewhat extensive, and I didn't quite understand. He goes straight to the area, and he issues assignments on the spot based on the commander's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If a company is in a position of coordinated action, if it is coordinating actions with a different unit, in preparation for this coordinated or concerted action, does the company commander have to agree with those units on the way in which the units are to be used in the sense of coordination, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sorting out how coordinated action should be taken implies that contact should be established at an equal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, if you have a platoon-level unit, a company commander can even decide to contact the platoon commander who is positioned along the same axis or in a neighbouring village, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then agree finally, and does it not follow logically by way of a conclusion, that it is precisely this observation post or wherever the company commander happens to be staying, or, rather, can he use this position to meet and agree coordinated action with other units such as we have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we also agree, and what would your answer be, a company commander has an order and a decision of the battalion commander, detailing the axes of attack. Higher level units are assigned so-called areas of responsibility or operations areas?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations areas or attack areas, whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just take a minute to think about this. When defending, they are assigned a sector; and when attacking, they are assigned an axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In your capacity as a military expert, can you please, to some extent, try to explain what this means, attack on a settled area. What does that term mean, what does that imply, as an aspect of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An attack on a settled area is an attack. Just like an attack is an attack whenever any building is attacked from the point of view of the other side, of the enemy. There are some peculiarities, needless to say. It is a settled area, we're talking about a populated area. It is fortified by virtue of being populated. There are fortifications also in the engineering sense of the word. You can have circular defence, that is always an option. There can be close-range combat, there can be ambush, that sort of thing. All these peculiarities must be familiar to the commander. And then the commander takes care of this. Under the rules, and on account of all these peculiarities, on account of the degree of difficulty involved, on account of the fact that large losses may be expected, the area is blocked or surrounded, and then the operation continues. But in this specific case, Vukovar should have been taken, and that is where the direct attack and direct involvement in the town itself arose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness seems on top form right now in terms of providing all these explanations, despite which I notice it is now time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I hope you don't lose your touch during the break. We will resume at a quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could we now discuss Captain Radic, please? Do you know what his function was during the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Radic was a company commander. Komandir, within the 1st Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also within the composition of the Assault Detachment No. 1, the 1st Battalion being part of that detachment. So he was within the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your stay in Vukovar, did you ever come to the axis of the attack of the 3rd Company in order to control the combat positions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was only at the command post of the Assault Detachment No. 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you said you were one of the staff at Negoslavci, did you hear of Captain Radojvic [as interpreted], in the way he commanded and controlled at his positions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything in particular, be it positive or negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Some witnesses mentioned that at the very beginning that he was left without his platoon commanders, which belonged to him by establishment. As a person who understands the topic, what sort of a person a company commander need be -- needs to be to be able to conduct combat operations without your platoon leaders? Did he have to be disciplined, decisive, or, rather, you can put it in your own words. What would a commander need to be without his platoon commanders?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a situation is a very difficult one for a person to command a company, and one needs exceptional ability to carry out the tasks assigned to a company commander, including all the elements that fall within his abilities, responsibility, taking initiative, discipline, continuous work, and that entailed great difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you provided to the OTP, there are some portions of it that were addressed by our learned friend from the OTP. I believe you have the statement before you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 20 of the statement, inter alia, and I can read it out. It states: "During the operations the Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica TO detachments were subordinated to the Guards Motorised Brigade in the area where they were located." That's the way it is stated here. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In these proceedings, it is no secret that their axis coincided with the axis of the 3rd Company commanded by Captain Radic. But within the 1st JOD, as you said yourself, being the 1st Assault Platoon commanded by Borivoje Tesic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: By the principle of subordination, who at the time commanded the units under the term -- the Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica TO units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the commander of the Assault Detachment No. 1, this being Borivoje Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 18th of November, perhaps we could agree that that's when the combat activities in Vukovar ceased?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether, on that day, there was no longer the need to have assault detachments and groups which were formed to carry out specific tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was no need anymore, provided the combat activities have been concluded, such as was the case. So their subordination could be dealt with immediately. They, at that point, could have been returned to their establishment units, but I don't think it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borivoje Tesic, who was commander of a battalion and commander of the 1st JOD, could he, based on his own decision, transfer TO units and the Leva Supoderica unit to various axes of combat activities within his area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar whether he was doing that, based on the decision by Colonel Mrksic as well, and Colonel Mrksic being the commander of OG South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what way he commanded in his part of the area. I presume that he had formed assault groups using his establishment companies and the detachments resubordinated to him within the area. I didn't see any of the orders issued to him. Or I may have, but I don't remember any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We will go through some of those orders at a later stage, and I believe you will be able to provide a precise answer to my question. If we go back to the previous question as to whether a company commander could make a decision concerning the use of TO units and the Leva Supoderica unit the way Borivoje Tesic could do, who was the commander of the 1st Assault Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The commander, company commander couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we also agree, perhaps, that the battalion commander, that is the commander of the 1st JOD, Mr. Tesic, de jure and de facto, had responsibility over the units of the TO and the Leva Supoderica unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I please kindly ask the usher to show us Exhibit 405 on the screen? It is tab 3. I've also distributed copies to the OTP and the Chamber. It is an order by the commander of the guards brigade to block and attack that was forwarded to the commanders of units within the 80th Motorised Brigade on the 1st of October, 1991. Could you be so kind as to read out something on page 2? That is item 5, "tasks of the units"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 1st Assault Detachment comprises the 1st Motorised Brigade with the 3rd Company" -- no, "the 3rd Platoon of the 1st Company of the armoured battalion, the 2nd Platoon of the 2nd Battery of the Light Self-propelled Artillery Battalion of air defence, and the 3rd Platoon of the 2nd Company of the military police, and pioneer squad, detachment commander of the 1st Motorised Brigade commander. Task: Bring up the infantry parts to the first sector to the achieved line during the night before first light on 2nd October, 1991, with guides from Petrova Gora TO unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would kindly ask the usher to put Exhibit 408 on the screen. This is tab 4. Your Honours, this is another decision by the commander of OG South dated the 15th of October, 1991. I would kindly ask the witness to read out item 2, subparagraph (a) mentioning the 1st JOD.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "JOD-1 structure: The 1st Motorised Brigade, the 3rd Platoon of the 1st Company" -- no, "the 3rd Squad of the 1st Company" -- no, "the 3rd Platoon of the 1st Company of the armoured battalion, the 1st Platoon of the 2nd Company of the military police battalion and one volunteer company from the current deployment continue the attack and in cooperation with the Assault Detachment No. 2 and the 3rd Battalion of the 211th Armoured Brigade and Petrova Gora units, crush the Ustasha units on the directions of: Vladimira Gacese Street, the 6th Proleterske Divizije settlement and Svetozara Markovica Street - 1 Maja Street, seize Hercegovacko Naselji and continue the attack, seize the 6th Proleterske Divizije and the 1 Maja Street, in that way create the conditions for the main forces to emerge into the centre of Vukovar."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now ask the usher to put Exhibit 410 on the screen, being tab 5. This is also a document of Operations Group South, the date being the 29th of October, 1991. I would again kindly ask the witness to read out item 2, "unit tasks," in particular of the 1st Assault Detachment commanded by Borivoje Tesic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Assault Detachment No. 1 comprises the 1st Motorised Battalion, the 1st Platoon of the 3rd Company of the 2nd Battalion of the military police, Leva Supoderica detachment, Petrova Gora detachment, Novi Sad volunteers company, 1 M-84 tank, 1st Squad of the 1st Pioneers Company, part of the Territorial Defence unit will continue the attack from the current sector in cooperation with JOD-2 and by the introduction of forces break up the Ustasha units in Cvetno and Pionirsko Naselje, break out into 1 Maja Street, and then, in cooperation with the 3rd Battalion of the 211th Armoured Brigade, continue the attack with the main forces in the area within reach of 1 Maja Street, and with auxiliary forces, break up the Ustasha forces in the 6th Proleterske Divizije housing estate."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on what you have read out and what you've said so far, as regards the use of the 1st Assault Detachment, who was responsible to the command of the 1st Military District for the use of TO units and the Leva Supoderica unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Assault Detachment No. 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This being Borivoje Tesic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Based on what you know, are you able to confirm that in the rules which exist and which you studied, and these are the rules for companies and platoons, the following is regulated: In order to execute combat assignment, a company can be reinforced up to platoon strength in weapons using recoilless canon, mortars of 82 millimetres. Just one moment please, so that we don't overlap. So recoilless guns, mortars of 82 millimetres, exceptionally with a battery of 120-millimetre mortars, an engineering platoon or pioneers platoon, some tanks, and in certain conditions by a platoon of TO units. The question is: Can you confirm that something like this exists in the military rules for platoons and companies?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us, and also compare for us, a platoon of the TO and a detachment of the TO in terms of numbers and the manner of use of either type of unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A TO detachment is at the level of a battalion of the Yugoslav People's Army. It can be a smaller force, and the weaponry can differ. It's mostly armed by light weapons. The establishment structure it has is the same. It's made up of companies of the TOs, the companies are made up of platoons, and there -- also have threefold formation there; three platoons, three companies, three battalions. With these reinforcements that you talked about, that's an option.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as for the strength, I've already said it wasn't up to the strength of a battalion. At that time it was 700, it can number fewer men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But can you agree with the assertion of the Defence that the 3rd Company, which was under the command of Radic, according to establishment, could not have had two detachments of the TO?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two -- two order -- two detachments of the TO, it couldn't have had a single one. According to the principle of resubordination, it was a question if it could have had a company, never mind this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So based on your answer, is it possible then to conclude that the commander of the 1st JOD could not have resubordinated these two TO detachments or as the friends from the Prosecution like to say, incorporate them into the 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That is impossible. It's the first time that I'm hearing of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Thank you. I would like to ask the usher to place e-court document number 000-0079, and in the English that would be number 0D00-0081. Could you please look at tab 1 now? This refers to a decision by the commander of OG South of the 14th of November, 1991. I would like to ask you to read paragraph 4, but please do this slowly because this is important, and then after that could you please read paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Assault attachment 1, without the 1st Motorised Battalion, from the current area of combat disposition relocate to the Dalmatinska Street-Alija Alijagica Street water-tower axis."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now read item 5?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "1st Motorised Battalion from the current region of combat disposition secure the reached line, establish full control over the captured area, and engage in coordinated action with the attack forces along the Sundariceva [phoen] Marsala Tita Street axis. Be on stand-by for active combat along the Milovo Brdo - bridges on the Vuka River axis."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will be exhibit number 430.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you be a little more exact, please. When you interpret for us what it says, JOD-1 in the order without the 1st Motorised Battalion, and could you please explain to the Trial Chamber, if possible, the idea of the OG commander to assign this task to Major Tesic. So these are two questions, actually.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion, Major Tesic, was the commander of the Assault Detachment 1. We concluded already what the composition of the detachment was. That included Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora. Two detachments. And the 1st Motorised Battalion. The commander decided that these TO units should take up this assignment, which we read in item 4, and that the first battalion of complete establishment formation should be entrusted with this second task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sub-question: The 1st Motorised Battalion, which is now on another task, does that mean that the entire battalion has three companies, including the company of Captain Radic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Its complete establishment composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that at that point in time Major Borivoje Tesic was at the same time the commander of the 1st JOD and commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion, regardless of the fact that these two parts were on different axes of attack, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All he needed to do was to regulate from within how this was supposed to function.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know as a witness that Major Tesic acted in accordance with the decision by the commander of OG South and did he have any particular reason not to adhere to the order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Had he had some problems, would Mr. Borivoje Tesic have informed the OG South commander at the first briefing at the OG South command briefing which he attended regularly, as you said?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall him informing about these particular difficulties, that the assignment he had been given was unrealistic. He did report on the difficulties that I talked about earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to ask the usher to place on the monitor document marked 0D02-442 [as interpreted], and the English version, 0D00-0444. We have a decision of the commander of OG South dated the 16th of November, 1991. I would now like to ask the witness to read items 1 and item -- items 1 and 2, please. This is in tab 2 for the Trial Chamber and my learned friends from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I have decided to continue the attack as per the previous decision by the main forces on the axis Milovo Brdo - the bridges on the Vuka River, and by auxiliary forces on the axis: Graveyard-Slavija-Vucedol-Mitnica with the necessary regroupings and by including newly arrived units in the combat operations for the purpose of: During 17th of November, 1991, cut off the main Ustasha forces and establish control over the central parts of town and narrow down the defence front of the Ustasha forces in Mitnica as much as possible." This is a combat disposition in accordance with the previous decision by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you read this more important part, tasks by the units, and this was -- could you please read item 1?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1: "1st Motorised Battalion, in line with the task of the 14th of November, 1991, with support of a part of the forces of the armoured battalion of the Guards Motorised Brigade, continued the attack on the axis of Sundariceva Street, Rade Koncara estate, bridges over the Vuka River and by 1600 hours on the 17th of November seize the area surrounding the bridges over the Vuka River, Marsala Tita Street, from which location they should be ready to continue the attack over the Republike square towards the Danube and Marsala Tita Street-Stjepana Radica Street."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Question: Why did the commander of OG South specify in this assignment of the 1st Motorised Brigade, and what does it mean, this thing that you read in accordance with the task of the 14th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This relates to this concept by the commander which I read in the -- in item 1, the reason is the need to regroup. Yes, I understand. You made a slip of the tongue, but I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is a slip of the tongue. On the 17th it says motorised brigade, but it should state motorised battalion. I probably made this mistake and even though this is quite clear, I would like to still have that cleared up for the transcript, that all the time we're talking about the motorised battalion. May I continue, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us about this particular time that we're talking about in accordance of all of these decisions? Who is in command of the Territorial Defence or the detachments of Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are under the command of the commander of Assault Detachment 1, Borivoje Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you, as somebody who is familiar with these things, do you know of any document, decision or order that you dealt with at the command post of OG South after the 6th [as interpreted] of November, 1991, which would considerably change the situation that we have seen from these documents in terms of responsibility over units of the TO Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica in the course of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as an exhibit, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 431, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another intervention for the transcript, in line 12 it says that it was the 6th of November, but I said the 16th of November. Also in the exhibit that I am tendering it can be seen that the date is the 16th of November, 1991. So please could you consider that a correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, in relation to a document by the Prosecution, the order on setting up the commands in the sectors, you read out in one of the paragraphs that the local commanders in the town of Vukovar were commanders of assault detachments, everyone in their own zones of responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Now you would like to talk about the Petrova Gora local commander. So this is tab 6 now. I would like to have Exhibit 418 placed on the monitor. And would you kindly, because at the request of my learned friend from the Prosecution you read about units of OG South, and you read three items out. I would now like you to read item 4, which actually relates to what I am asking you about. So this would be item 4, page 2, in tab 6.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "The following were appointed for the commanders of liberated Vukovar: For Vucedol and Mitnica, Major Miroslav Stupar. For Petrova Gora and the western part of the graveyard up to the Vuka River, Major Borivoje Tesic. For the part of Vukovar from the Sajmiste Street east to Mitnica, Major Adem Bajic."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, there is no need to read anymore. In the transcript of May 3rd, page 8.091, you spoke generally about the assignments and duties of local commanders, also including Borivoje Tesic, who was the commander of Petrova Gora, and we're talking about the same order. So my question is: If Major Tesic had a platoon of military police subordinated to him, could he have used that platoon in order to set up military authority to introduce discipline, prevent looting and prevent abuses of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was exactly the means he should have used in order to deal with those problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ovcara was in the zone of responsibility of the 80th Motorised Brigade, and in your testimony here, and also in the indictment in paragraph 60 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Said in your statement, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that on the 21st Mrksic issued an order underlining the responsibility of all the commanders for the complete functioning of authority in line with his previous order.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Is that true? Is this accurate, what I have just suggested to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does this not mean that the local commander of Ovcara, Jakubovac and Grabovo should have complete control over his area?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both complete control and full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What we really want to know is this: He was supposed to have full and effective control over all units in that area, the area under him, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the military police of the 80th Kragujevac Motorised Brigade withdrew on the 20th of November, at about 2230 hours. They withdrew from Ovcara, from outside the hangar. Are you familiar with that? I can tell you that this is something that is known to the Defence, but it's not something that you testified about. I'm suggesting this to you as a hypothesis, as a possibility. What would that mean? The military police company of the 80th Kragujevac Motorised Brigade withdrew. Would that still mean that Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic was still responsible for Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have two or three questions left, Your Honour. Can I go on now? Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We heard a witness at this trial, this witness made a statement and gave evidence. He said that at these official meetings at Operations Group South he used to see Miroslav Radic. He claims that Miroslav Radic came to these meetings from time to time. The reference, for the benefit of the Chamber and the OTP, is witness number 70 on the 65 ter list. This witness has not been heard, actually. I think there is an error in the transcript. I'm not specifying the witness, but this is under the hypothesis that he will say the same thing that he already said in his statement to the Prosecutor. He also stated that Captain Radic was a commander of a military police company. Can you please tell us, Witness, firstly, in his potential capacity or alleged capacity as company commander would he have been entitled to attend these staff meetings; and secondly, was he a company -- was he commander of a military political company at all. Do you know what this witness was trying to tell us, at all?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radic only came once to the command post in Negoslavci, and he was barred from entering the operations room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is clear whether he was an MP company commander or a motorised company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And what would the answer to that one be?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He commanded a motorised company. That much is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Another witness stated that he returned his PM machine-gun at a police-manned check-point at the entrance to Negoslavci. He also said that he had received an certificate from the officer from the guards brigade called R. Zunic, a major by rank. Firstly, do you know a major by that name who belonged to the motorised guards brigade. If so, was it possible for such a major at a check-point to issue certificates for weapons that were being returned with the following military post number, 4795-2. The reference for the Prosecutor and the Chamber is Exhibit 197, so that we're on the same page.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zunic was not a major by rank. Captain First Class at best. He was a member of the 1st Battalion of the military police. The 1st Battalion of the military police had two assignments, not to mention the third when they got involved in combat operations, to inspect and secure their area and to provide security for the command post. In terms of securing the area, they set up check-points. Now, as to whether Captain or Lieutenant Zunic was at this check-point that this witness suggested, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And my second question: Was he in a position to rubber-stamp certificates with a specific military post number right there, in case he was there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This was down to the security bodies. They were the ones who organised this. And this was an operative segment of their work. They probably were authorised to endorse and rubber-stamp such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I see you're not being specific, and to keep you from speculating any further on this issue, I'll just move on to my next question. P-021, Witness P-021, states -- P-022. It's an error in the transcript. It says 021. P-022 states that Croats were ordered not to go to Vukovar. Or, to be quite specific, on page 4949, line 24, the witness stated that before they set out for Vukovar, and he means the guards brigade, all the Croat soldiers were set aside, and when the alert was given, the military police sent them to one side. I've heard what you had to say about this. Would that mean that this is just not true, and that no Croat soldiers were singled out from the rest and there was no order like that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is just not true. I can explain if you would like me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role of the security battalion had specific buildings that they had to secure. Some elements had to be used to secure the barracks and for regular military security jobs. This applied to all the various structures in the barracks. Some of the soldiers were left behind, and this had nothing to do with ethnic criteria. Ethnic criteria were not regarded. What I told the OTP, there were lots of Croatian soldiers, even officers, of course that's what I mean, involved in combat in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This same witness, P-022, on page 5151, line 16, stated this: Captain Dragan, and he means Bundzulic, had the task of securing the house in which Captain Radic slept. First of all, do you know who Captain Dragan Bundzulic was, and what was his role in Vukovar, which were the units in his command? Can you help us with?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bundzulic, as for our motorised battalions, we had 120-millimetre mortars, we had a battery. He was a member of the crew of that particular 120-millimetre battery. I'm not sure if he was the commander of the particular crew or battery or one of the platoon commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That seems to be that what the witness suggested is not true when he said that the commander of this unit could have potentially provided security for Captain Radic's house there or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the principles, and if you look at the disposition of the units, the combat disposition, not a chance in hell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Another question, I think my last question.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: True enough, I'm talking about an artillery unit. So artillery observers are normally closer to the position an attacking unit. They observe fire, they send feedback to the firing positions so that adjustments may be made. If this was the case, the battery commander, in case he was also in charge of observing, could possibly have been physically closer to Captain Radic's observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. But quite specifically, could that unit have been used for securing the house in which Captain Radic was sleeping all the time or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because the firing position was far behind and the army was right there, and what we're talking about here is something totally different unless he was personally providing security around that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Based on everything that you just told us, was Captain Radic able, Captain Radic as a company commander within the Vukovar operation, could he have his own headquarters conducting the liberation of Vukovar? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies Your Honours, I have concluded, but this was in reference to evidence of a witness back in 1996, page 3, paragraph 4, it was a statement made to the OTP, that's the English reference. And the witness is P-002 [as interpreted]. He will be heard shortly by the Chamber, I believe. But he spoke a great deal about this, and I believe for the sake of a fair trial I am entitled to point this out to the Chamber, since I believe that to be erroneous. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Borovic. Well, I think we've probably come to a convenient time. Just to let Mr. Bulatovic off the hook. We will adjourn for the weekend. We resume on Monday at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of May, 2006, at 12.00 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
